instruction: FBX for Unity (Y-up, meters, animation enabled). `scene.blend` contains one animated 1x1x1 m mesh object named `Cube` at the origin. Its location is (0, 0, 0) at frame 1 and (0, 0, 2) at frame 30, so it rises 2 m along Z. The scene uses Metric units in meters with Unit Scale 1.0 and spans frames 1 through 30. Export the scene from Blender's FBX export dialog as `/home/user/Desktop/part.fbx`, overwriting any existing file. Use the following Unity-friendly export settings: Apply Scalings = FBX Units Scale; Forward = -Z Forward; Up = Y Up; Bake Animation enabled; NLA Strips disabled; All Actions disabled; Force Start/End Keying enabled. Export all objects rather than only selected objects, and include Mesh, Armature, and Empty object types. Use the default binary FBX format with the animation embedded. Requirements: 1. `part.fbx` is a readable, non-empty binary FBX file in FBX 2014 format or newer. 2. Its global up axis is Y. 3. Its unit scale is 100 centimetres per meter, preserving the scene's one-unit-per-meter scale for Unity. 4. It contains an animation stack and baked animation curves retaining the `Cube` motion from frames 1 through 30.
